rules.question: What is the 2025 corporate income tax rate?
rules.whyItMatters: Schedule J line 1a is a flat 21% of taxable income; there are no brackets.

rules.excerpt: Line 1a. Income tax. Multiply taxable income (page 1, line 30) by 21% (0.21). Enter this amount on line 1a.

rules.hangsApplication: Taxable income of $60,241.87 times 21% is $12,650.79, the total tax on line 31. The rate was 21% for every day of the fiscal year, so no blended rate is figured; no credits and no corporate alternative minimum tax.

rules.question: When is the return for a fiscal year ending June 30, 2026 due?

rules.excerpt: Generally, a corporation must file its income tax return by the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of its tax year ... However, a corporation with a fiscal tax year ending June 30 must file by the 15th day of the 3rd month after the end of its tax year.

rules.question: Is the business interest limited?

rules.question: What did HANGS have to pay in each 2025 installment?
rules.whyItMatters: Each installment is 25% of the smaller of the 2025 tax and the 2024 tax (from a full 12-month return showing tax); a large corporation can use last year's tax only for its first installment.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty; Part II line 8; Part III line 9.
rules.excerpt: Generally, a corporation is subject to the penalty if it did not timely pay at least the smaller of: the tax shown on its 2025 return, or the tax shown on its 2024 return (if it filed a 2024 return showing at least some amount of tax and the return was for a full 12 months). ... A large corporation is a corporation ... that had ... taxable income ... of $1 million or more for any of the 3 tax years immediately preceding the 2025 tax year ... The corporation is generally required to enter the 15th day of the 4th ... 6th, 9th, and 12th months of its tax year.

rules.question: How is the penalty for the short September installment figured?
rules.whyItMatters: The penalty runs from the installment's due date until the shortfall is paid; a later payment goes first to the earliest unpaid installment.
